subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migration, should OpenClaw reset/scope update offsets by apiRoot in runtime, rely on doctor/docs for manual reset, or keep account/token-only offsets as an operator-managed advanced workflow?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing persisted offset identity and tolerating a specific 400 startup error are compatibility-sensitive runtime choices that should match maintainer intent.

options.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
options.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when apiRoot changes, add a narrow logged-out deleteWebhook tolerance, and require live local Bot API migration proof.

options.title: Doctor/docs reset only
options.body: Keep runtime offsets account/token-scoped and make doctor or documentation the supported path to reset offsets when switching endpoints.

options.title: Keep current advanced workflow
options.body: Leave local Bot API endpoint migration operator-managed and document manual cleanup expectations without runtime offset changes.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
recommendation.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when apiRoot changes, add a narrow logged-out deleteWebhook tolerance, and require live local Bot API migration proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on Telegram polling/spool and offset account-id handling makes this the best available routing candidate for the runtime decision.
